dervis-irab:6-8.t:
* I'rab:
(النَّبِيُّ أَوْلى بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ): (النبي) is the mubtadaʾ (subject), (أولى بالمؤمنين) is the khabar (predicate), and (من أنفسهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, likewise attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أولى). (وَأَزْواجُهُ أُمَّهاتُهُمْ وَأُولُوا الْأَرْحامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلى بِبَعْضٍ فِي كِتابِ اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُهاجِرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (أزواجه) is a mubtadaʾ and (أمهاتهم) its khabar — the meaning of this simile will come in the section on rhetoric. (أولو الأرحام) is also a mubtadaʾ; (الأرحام) is the plural of (رحم), meaning kinship. (بعضهم) is a second mubtadaʾ, or a badal (substitute) from (أولو), and (أولى ببعض) is the khabar; an omitted muḍāf must be assumed, i.e. "with respect to inheriting from one another". (في كتاب الله) is attached to (أولى), or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (أولى). (من المؤمنين) is a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to (أولى); that is, blood relatives are more entitled to inherit from one another than that the unrelated believers and emigrants should inherit from them. You may also attach it to an omitted ḥāl, since it serves as a clarification of His saying (أولو الأرحام).
(إِلَّا أَنْ تَفْعَلُوا إِلى أَوْلِيائِكُمْ مَعْرُوفاً كانَ ذلِكَ فِي الْكِتابِ مَسْطُوراً): (إلا) is a particle of exception, and (أن تفعلوا) is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), excepted from the most general of the general, because it is an exception from a different genus, i.e. "except in the bequest", which is what is meant by doing a kindness. (إلى أوليائكم) is attached to (تفعلوا), after it has been made to include the sense of (تؤدوا) "you render" or (تسدوا) "you bestow". (معروفا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (كان) with its noun, and (مسطورا) is its khabar; (في الكتاب) is attached to (مسطورا).
(وَإِذْ أَخَذْنا مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ مِيثاقَهُمْ وَمِنْكَ وَمِنْ نُوحٍ وَإِبْراهِيمَ وَمُوسى وَعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ): the adverb is attached to an omitted verb, i.e. "remember", and the speech is resumptive. You may also conjoin it to the position of (في الكتاب), so that it is attached to (مسطورا); but the first is preferable. The clause (أخذنا) is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it. (من النبيين) is attached to (أخذنا), and (ميثاقهم) is the mafʿūl bihi; what is meant by it is conveying the message. What follows is conjoined to (من النبيين), as a conjoining of the particular to the general, as will come in the section on rhetoric.
(وَأَخَذْنا مِنْهُمْ مِيثاقاً غَلِيظاً): conjoined to the preceding (أخذنا); the secret of describing the covenant as "firm/thick" will come in the section on rhetoric. (لِيَسْئَلَ الصَّادِقِينَ عَنْ صِدْقِهِمْ وَأَعَدَّ لِلْكافِرِينَ عَذاباً أَلِيماً): the lām is of cause; (يسأل) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) (أن) after the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (أخذ), by way of iltifāt (shift of person). Its fāʿil (agent) is a latent pronoun referring to Allah. (الصادقين) is the mafʿūl bihi, and (عن صدقهم) is attached to (يسأل). (وأعد للكافرين) is conjoined to (أخذنا من النبيين); (للكافرين) is attached to (أعد), (عذابا) is the mafʿūl bihi, and (أليما) is an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
1- The eloquent simile (al-tashbīh al-balīgh):
In His saying «وأزواجه أمهاتهم» there is an eloquent simile, and the point of similarity is multiple, relating to certain rulings: the obligation to honour and respect them and the prohibition of marrying them. That is why ʿĀʾisha said: «We are not the mothers of the women», meaning that they were only the mothers of the men, inasmuch as they were forbidden to them just as their mothers are forbidden. For this reason the particle of comparison must be assumed in it.
2- Conjoining the particular to the general:
In His saying «وإذا أخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم ومنك» [Translator's note: the source writes «وإذا»; the verse reads «وَإِذْ أَخَذْنا»] — the verse — there is a conjoining of the particular to the general, because these five who are mentioned are the possessors of the revealed laws and the scriptures, and the resolute among the messengers (ulū al-ʿazm), so He singled them out for mention to draw attention to the eminence of their merit over others. He put the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ first, although he comes after Noah and those after him, because he is the one addressed among them and the one to whom this recited text was revealed; so putting him first was for this reason, not because precedence in mention requires that he be the most excellent of them. For it has come in poetry:
بهاليل منهم جعفر وابن أمه ... علي ومنهم أحمد المتخير
(Noble chiefs: among them Jaʿfar and his mother's son ʿAlī, and among them Aḥmad the chosen one.)
So the poet placed the mention of the Prophet last, in order to close with him as an honour.
3- The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya):
In describing the covenant as "thick" (غليظ) there is an implicit metaphor: He likened the covenant to a tangible body and borrowed for it one of the attributes of bodies, namely thickness, to draw attention to the greatness and majesty of the covenant. This is the one meant by His saying, the Exalted: «وإذا أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين لما آتيتكم من كتاب وحكمة» — the verse. [Translator's note: the verse (Āl ʿImrān 3:81) reads «وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ»; the source writes «وإذا».]

dervis-irab:53-53.t:
* Vocabulary:
(إِناهُ), with kasra or fatḥa on the hamza: the arrival of the time, and ripeness. It is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of أنى يأني, that is, a maṣdar known by hearing (samāʿī), because it belongs to the pattern of رمى, and the analogical form of its maṣdar would be أني, like رمي; but that is not attested. What is attested is إنى, with kasra and the short alif, on the pattern of رضا.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ): a resumptive statement, introduced to begin explaining what people are obliged to observe regarding the rights of the Prophet's wives. لا is prohibitive; تدخلوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; بيوت النبي is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa).
(إِلَّا أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ إِلى طَعامٍ غَيْرَ ناظِرِينَ إِناهُ): إلا is a particle of restriction, and the maṣdar أن يؤذن is an "emptied" exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh) from the most general of states, i.e. do not enter them in any state whatsoever except the state of your having been given permission. Al-Zamakhsharī chose that it be an emptied exception from the most general of adverbs of time, i.e. they are not to enter them at any time except the time when permission is given to you, and his choice is not far-fetched.
يؤذن is a passive imperfect verb; لكم is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يؤذن, and likewise إلى طعام, because يؤذن includes the sense of invitation. Al-Samīn also chose that the maṣdar be in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. except by reason of permission being given to you, the bāʾ being causal. غير ناظرين is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of لا تدخلوا; the exception falls on the adverb and the ḥāl together, as if it were said: do not enter the houses of the Prophet except at the time of permission, and do not enter them except not waiting. إناه, i.e. its ripeness, is a mafʿūl bihi of ناظرين. They were people who used to watch for the time of the Messenger of Allah's food, then enter and sit waiting for it to be ready.
(وَلكِنْ إِذا دُعِيتُمْ فَادْخُلُوا فَإِذا طَعِمْتُمْ فَانْتَشِرُوا وَلا مُسْتَأْنِسِينَ لِحَدِيثٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), lightened and inoperative; إذا is an adverb of the future, and the clause دعيتم is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. فادخلوا: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ, and ادخلوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent). فإذا: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and the clause طعمتم is the muḍāf ilayhi of the adverb. فانتشروا is the apodosis of إذا. ولا مستأنسين: the wāw is a conjunction, لا is negative, and مستأنسين is conjoined to غير ناظرين. It is also said to be conjoined to an implied ḥāl, i.e. do not enter them barging in nor lingering. Al-Zamakhsharī and others chose that it is genitive, conjoined to ناظرين. لحديث is attached to مستأنسين; the lām is causal, i.e. lingering so that you may talk with one another. It may also be the lām that strengthens the governing word, i.e. nor lingering for the talk of the household and others.
(إِنَّ ذلِكُمْ كانَ يُؤْذِي النَّبِيَّ فَيَسْتَحْيِي مِنْكُمْ وَاللَّهُ لا يَسْتَحْيِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ): the clause gives the reason for the prohibition. إنّ is a particle resembling the verb, ذلكم is its noun, and the clause كان يؤذي النبي is its khabar (predicate); the reference is to staying and lingering. The clause يؤذي النبي is the khabar of كان. فيستحيي is conjoined to يؤذي, and منكم is attached to it; a muḍāf must be supplied, i.e. of sending you out. The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause لا يستحيي من الحق is its khabar. What is meant by the truth is sending them out. The meaning of this proverbial expression will come in the Rhetoric section.
(وَإِذا سَأَلْتُمُوهُنَّ مَتاعاً فَسْئَلُوهُنَّ مِنْ وَراءِ حِجابٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb for future time, and the clause سألتموهن is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. فاسألوهن: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ, and اسألوهن is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi. متاعا is the second mafʿūl bihi of سأل, and من وراء حجاب is attached to اسألوهن.
(ذلِكُمْ أَطْهَرُ لِقُلُوبِكُمْ وَقُلُوبِهِنَّ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ, i.e. what has been mentioned of not entering without permission, not lingering for talk, and asking for goods from behind a screen. أطهر is the khabar; لقلوبكم is attached to أطهر, and قلوبهن is conjoined to قلوبكم.
(وَما كانَ لَكُمْ أَنْ تُؤْذُوا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَلا أَنْ تَنْكِحُوا أَزْواجَهُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ أَبَداً): the wāw is resumptive; ما is negative; كان is a defective past verb; لكم is its fronted khabar; أن and what falls within its scope form an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the nominative as its postponed noun. رسول الله is a mafʿūl bihi. ولا أن تنكحوا is conjoined to أن تؤذوا; أزواجه is a mafʿūl bihi; من بعده is a ḥāl; أبدا is an adverb.
(إِنَّ ذلِكُمْ كانَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ عَظِيماً): إن and its noun; the reference is to what has been mentioned of harming him and marrying his wives after him. The clause كان is the khabar of إن; the noun of كان is latent (mustatir); عظيما is the khabar; عند الله is attached to an omitted ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
Majāz (figurative usage) in His words «والله لا يستحيي من الحق»; the relation of this figure is causality, because whoever is shy of something usually leaves it. The speech runs as a proverb, so as to be a lesson in manners by which tiresome guests are admonished. How beautiful is the saying of ʿĀʾisha: «حسبك في الثقلاء أن الله تعالى لم يحتملهم» ("Enough for you concerning tiresome people is that Allah the Exalted did not put up with them").

dervis-irab:9-13.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْحَناجِرَ): plural of (حنجرة), which is the throat (الحلقوم), or the top of the epiglottis (الغلصمة), which is the end of the throat. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «They said: when the lungs swell from intense fright, anger or severe distress, they expand, and the heart rises with their rising up to the top of the throat; hence it is said of a coward "his lungs have swelled" (انتفخ سحره). It may also be a figure for the agitation and pounding of hearts, even if they did not literally reach the throats.»
(زِلْزالًا): with kasra on the zāy, which is the common reading; fatḥa is also permissible, since these are two dialectal forms of the maṣdar of the doubled verb when it comes on the pattern فعلان, such as زلزال, قلقال and صلصال. The form with fatḥa may be intended as an active participle, such as صلصال meaning مصلصل and زلزال meaning مزلزل.
(يَثْرِبَ): In al-Qāmūs: «Yathrib and Athrib: the city of the Prophet ﷺ; one says Yathrabī and Athrabī, with fatḥa or kasra on the rāʾ in both.» It is said it was named after a man of the Amalekites who settled there in ancient times; and it is said Yathrib is the name of the city itself. The Prophet forbade that it be called by this name because of what it contains of tathrīb, which is reproach and rebuke; so they mentioned it by this name in opposition to the Prophet. In al-Mukhtār: tathrīb is upbraiding and going to the limit in blame; ثرب عليه تثريبا means he denounced his deed to him.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ جاءَتْكُمْ جُنُودٌ): (اذكروا) is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); (نعمة الله) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (عليهم) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has (عليكم)] is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نعمة), or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (إذ) is an adverb of past time, attached to (اذكروا); it is thus in the position of a badal al-ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from (نعمة الله). What is meant by the blessing is His help in the Battle of the Confederates (al-Aḥzāb), whose account will come in the section on benefits. The clause (جاءتكم جنود) is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it. (فَأَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحاً وَجُنُوداً لَمْ تَرَوْها وَكانَ اللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيراً): (فأرسلنا) is conjoined to (جاءتكم); (عليهم) is attached to (أرسلنا); (ريحا) is the mafʿūl bihi and (جنودا) is conjoined to (ريحا); the clause (لم تروها) is an adjective of (جنودا). (كان الله): (كان) and its noun; (بما) is attached to (بصيرا); the clause (تعملون) is the ṣila (relative clause), and (بصيرا) is the khabar (predicate) of (كان). (إِذْ جاؤُكُمْ مِنْ فَوْقِكُمْ وَمِنْ أَسْفَلَ مِنْكُمْ): the adverb is a badal from (إذ جاءتكم); the clause (جاءوكم) is the muḍāf ilayhi; (من فوقكم) is attached to (جاءوكم), and (من أسفل منكم) is conjoined to (من فوقكم).
(وَإِذْ زاغَتِ الْأَبْصارُ وَبَلَغَتِ الْقُلُوبُ الْحَناجِرَ وَتَظُنُّونَ بِاللَّهِ الظُّنُونَا): conjoined to the preceding (إذ); likewise (بلغت القلوب الحناجر) and (تظنون بالله الظنونا). (الظنونا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the alif is added, treating the verse-endings like rhymes. The secret of the plural, together with the grammarians' views on the plural of the maṣdar, will come in the section on benefits.
(هُنالِكَ ابْتُلِيَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَزُلْزِلُوا زِلْزالًا شَدِيداً): (هنالك) is a demonstrative in the position of an accusative as an adverb of place; the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. It is attached to (ابتلي), and it may also be an adverb of time. (ابتلي) is a past verb in the passive, and (المؤمنون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (زلزلوا) is conjoined to (ابتلي), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil. (زلزالا) is a maṣdar clarifying the kind, and (شديدا) is an adjective. (وَإِذْ يَقُولُ الْمُنافِقُونَ وَالَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ ما وَعَدَنَا اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ إِلَّا غُرُوراً): the adverb is attached to an omitted (اذكر); the clause (يقول) is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it. (الذين) is conjoined to (المنافقون); (في قلوبهم) is a fronted khabar and (مرض) a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause (ما وعدنا) is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying); (الله) is the fāʿil and (رسوله) is conjoined to it; (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and (غرورا) is an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "except a promise of delusion".
(وَإِذْ قالَتْ طائِفَةٌ مِنْهُمْ يا أَهْلَ يَثْرِبَ لا مُقامَ لَكُمْ فَارْجِعُوا): conjoined to what precedes. (قالت طائفة) is a verb and its fāʿil; (منهم) is an adjective of (طائفة); (يا) is a vocative particle and (أهل يثرب) is a muḍāf vocative (munādā). (يثرب) is a diptote (barred from tanwīn) because it is a proper name and on the pattern of a verb, and it also carries femininity. (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (مقام) is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, and (لكم) is its khabar. (مقام) is read with ḍamma or fatḥa on the mīm, i.e. no residing and no standing place. (فارجعوا): the fāʾ is al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that reveals an implied condition), i.e. "if you heed my advice, then go back". The speaker was Aws ibn Qayẓī — with kasra on the ẓāʾ — one of the leaders of the hypocrites.
(وَيَسْتَأْذِنُ فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمُ النَّبِيَّ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّ بُيُوتَنا عَوْرَةٌ وَما هِيَ بِعَوْرَةٍ إِنْ يُرِيدُونَ إِلَّا فِراراً): (ويستأذن): the wāw is resumptive, and (يستأذن فريق) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. You may also conjoin it to what precedes, so that the imperfect form serves to make the scene present. (منهم) is an adjective of (فريق), and (النبي) is the mafʿūl bihi. The clause (يقولون) is a ḥāl, or explicative of (يستأذن) — and that is a fine view. The clause of (إن) with what falls in its domain is the maqūl al-qawl: (إن) with its noun and its khabar. What is meant by (عورة) is the weakness that makes them exposed to the enemy, since they are unfortified. The wāw is circumstantial; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negating mā, (هي) is its noun, the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (عورة) is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of (ما). (إن) is negating; (يريدون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and (فرارا) is the mafʿūl bihi.

* Benefits:
1- The Battle of the Confederates (al-Aḥzāb):
The Battle of the Confederates took place in Shawwāl of the year four — it is also said the year five — corresponding to March 627 CE, when an army of about ten thousand men moved against Medina, among them four thousand of Quraysh under the command of Abū Sufyān. The movement of this army was exceptionally swift this time. Its cause, as the historians mention, was that when the Banū al-Naḍīr were expelled from their homes, a group of their notables, among them their chief Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab, went until they came to Quraysh in Mecca and incited them to make war on the Messenger of Allah, saying: "We will be with you against him until we uproot him." Abū Sufyān said: "Welcome! The dearest of people to us is whoever helps us in our enmity towards Muhammad." Then Quraysh said to those Jews: "O company of Jews, you are the people of the first scripture, so tell us: are we in the right, or Muhammad?"
They said: "Rather, you are in the right." Regarding this stance of the Jews towards Quraysh, and their preferring Quraysh's idolatry over Muhammad, Dr. Israel Wolfensohn says in his book «The History of the Jews in the Lands of the Arabs»: «It was the duty of these Jews not to fall into such a gross error, and not to declare before the leaders of Quraysh that idol-worship was better than Islamic monotheism, even if this led to their request not being answered; for the Children of Israel, who for many centuries had been the bearers of the banner of monotheism in the world among the pagan nations in the name of the ancient patriarchs, and who were struck by countless calamities of killing and persecution because of their belief in one God in various ages of history, had the duty to sacrifice their lives and everything dear to them in order to thwart the polytheists. This is besides the fact that by resorting to the idol-worshippers they were only fighting themselves with their own hands and contradicting the teachings of the Torah, which enjoin them to shun the people of idols and to take a hostile stance towards them.»
Inciting the tribes and rallying them:
What Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab and the Jews with him said to Quraysh in preferring its idolatry to Muhammad's monotheism, so that it would be roused to fight him, did not suffice them. Rather, those Jews went out to Ghaṭafān of Qays ʿAylān, to Banū Murra, Banū Fazāra, Ashjaʿ, Sulaym, Banū Saʿd, Asad, and to all who had a blood-feud with the Muslims, and they kept inciting them to take their revenge, mentioning to them that Quraysh had joined them in the war against Muhammad, praising their idolatry and promising them certain victory. And the Confederates whom the Jews had gathered went out to fight Muhammad and his Companions.
What could the Muslims possibly do to face the thousands upon thousands of men, horses, camels, weapons and supplies? They had no way but to fortify themselves in virgin Yathrib — and yet?! Would this fortification suffice against that crushing force? Salmān al-Fārisī knew methods of war that were not known in the land of the Arabs, so he advised digging the trench around Medina and fortifying its interior. The Muslims hastened to carry out his advice: the trench was dug, and the Prophet worked in it with his own hand, carrying the earth, thereby encouraging the Muslims in the greatest way. Quraysh and its confederates came, hoping to meet Muhammad at Uḥud, but they found no one there, so they passed on to Medina until the trench took them by surprise. They were astonished, for they had not expected this kind of defence unknown to them, and their rage reached the point that they claimed sheltering behind it was a cowardice the Arabs had never known. Quraysh and the confederates with it saw that there was no way to cross the trench, so they contented themselves with exchanging volleys of arrows for several days.
Abū Sufyān and those with him became certain that they would be stationed before Yathrib and its trench for a long time without being able to storm it. The season was then winter, with biting cold and storming winds, its rain feared at every moment. While it was easy for the people of Mecca and Ghaṭafān to shelter from all that in their homes in Mecca and in Ghaṭafān, the tents they had pitched before Yathrib protected them from it not one whit. Moreover, they had come hoping for an easy victory that would cost them no more than a day like the day of Uḥud, after which they would return home and enjoy dividing the spoils and plunder. And what could keep Ghaṭafān from going home, when it had joined the war only because the Jews had promised it, once victory was achieved, a whole year's fruit from the farms and orchards of Khaybar — and here it saw victory was not easy, or at least not certain, and that it required, in this biting season, hardship enough to make it forget the fruits and orchards?
As for Quraysh's revenge for itself for Badr and the defeats that befell it after Badr, that could be attained in the course of time, so long as this trench prevented seizing Muhammad by the collar, and so long as the Banū Qurayẓa supplied the people of Yathrib with provisions in a way that would prolong their resistance for months upon months. Was it not better, then, for the Confederates to go home?
Yes — but gathering these confederates to fight Muhammad another time would not be easy, and if Muhammad triumphed through the withdrawal of the Confederates, woe to the Jews! Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab weighed all this and feared its consequences, and he saw that he had no choice but to venture his last arrow. So he suggested to the Confederates that he would persuade the Banū Qurayẓa to break their treaty of peace with Muhammad and the Muslims and to join them, and that once Qurayẓa did so, supplies and provisions would be cut off from Muhammad on one side, and the road would be opened for entering Yathrib on the other. He hastened to go seeking Kaʿb ibn Asad, the holder of the Banū Qurayẓa's pact, and kept at him until he opened the door of the fortress, and said to him:
"Woe to you, Kaʿb! I have brought you the glory of all time and a brimming sea: I have brought you Quraysh and Ghaṭafān, and they have pledged to me not to leave until we uproot Muhammad and those with him." Kaʿb hesitated, recalling Muhammad's faithfulness and his truthfulness to his pact, and feared the consequences of what Ḥuyayy was calling him to. But Ḥuyayy kept at him, reminding him of what had befallen the Jews at Muhammad's hands and what was about to befall them from him if the Confederates did not succeed in destroying him, until Kaʿb softened towards him and asked him: "And what will happen if the Confederates turn back?" Thereupon Ḥuyayy gave him a pledge that if Ghaṭafān and Quraysh went back without striking Muhammad, he would enter his fortress with him, support him and share his lot. Kaʿb's Jewishness stirred within him, so he accepted what Ḥuyayy asked, broke his pact with Muhammad and the Muslims, and abandoned his neutrality.
The morale of the Confederates rose until it drove some horsemen of Quraysh — among them ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Wudd, ʿIkrima ibn Abī Jahl and Ḍirār ibn al-Khaṭṭāb — to storm the trench. They made for a narrow place in it and spurred their horses, which carried them across into the salt-marsh between the trench and Salʿ. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib went out with a band of Muslims and seized against them the gap through which they had driven their horses. ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Wudd came forward calling: "Who will duel?" When ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib called him to single combat, he said arrogantly: "Go back, son of my brother, for by Allah I do not wish to kill you." ʿAlī said: "But by Allah I do wish to kill you." So they fought, and ʿAlī killed him, and the Confederates' horsemen fled in defeat until they crossed the trench again, turning their backs, heeding nothing.
The Confederates made their fires huge, to frighten the Muslims all the more and to weaken their spirits [Translator's note: the source has «لووحهم», evidently a misprint for «لروحهم»], and the zealots of Qurayẓa began coming down from their fortresses and strongholds into Medina and its houses near them, wanting to terrorise its people. Ṣafiyya bint ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib was in Fāriʿ, the fortress of Ḥassān ibn Thābit, and Ḥassān was in it with the women and children. A Jew passed by them, and Ṣafiyya said, addressing Ḥassān: "This Jew is circling the fortress; go down to him and kill him." Ḥassān said: "May Allah forgive you, daughter of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib! You know I am not the man for this." So Ṣafiyya took a post, went down from the fortress, and struck the Jew with it until she killed him. When she returned she said: "Ḥassān, go down to him and strip him, for nothing kept me from stripping him except that he is a man." Ḥassān said: "I have no need of his spoils."
The people of Medina remained in their fright, while Muhammad ﷺ began to think about the means of deliverance. The means was not, by the nature of the situation [Translator's note: the source has «بطبيعة الحيلة», apparently for «بطبيعة الحال»], to confront the enemy; so let it be stratagem, and let it be counsel and planning. He sent to Ghaṭafān promising them a third of the fruits of Medina if they would depart. Ghaṭafān had begun to grow weary, and showed resentment at the length of this siege and the hardship they had met during it. When night came, a violent wind blew, rain poured down, thunder crashed and the storm intensified, uprooting the Confederates' tents and casting terror into their souls. It seemed to them that the Muslims had begun an attack on them, so Ṭulayḥa ibn Khuwayla [Translator's note: so in the source; the usual form is Ṭulayḥa ibn Khuwaylid] stood up and called: "Muhammad has begun an attack on you — save yourselves!" Abū Sufyān said: "O company of Quraysh, by Allah you are no longer in a place to stay. The horses and camels have perished, the Banū Qurayẓa have failed us and we have heard from them what we dislike, and we have met from the violence of the wind what you see. So depart, for I am departing." The people took what light goods they could and set off, and Ghaṭafān followed them, so that when morning came Muhammad found none of them. He turned back to Medina, the Muslims with him raising their palms in supplication, giving thanks that Allah had lifted harm from them and that Allah had spared the believers the hardship of fighting. When the Confederates had cleared away, the Messenger of Allah said: "Now we will raid them, and they will not raid us." The rest is in the biographies and the lengthy works.
2- Is the maṣdar made dual and plural?
The maṣdar that emphasises its governing verb is not made dual or plural, by agreement [Translator's note: the source has «بانفاق», a misprint for «باتفاق»]. One does not say ضربت ضربين nor ضربت ضروبا, because it is an indefinite generic noun, and an indefinite maṣdar does not admit being joined to something else, since it denotes the bare reality, and the reality, as a reality, denotes little and much alike; so nothing remains that could be joined to it so that dual and plural would be valid in it. This is a rational matter. The maṣdar ending in tāʾ may be made dual and plural only because, by the entry of the tāʾ, it has come to denote a single instance of that maṣdar, so it can be joined to another single instance of it, and is thus made dual and plural. There is disagreement about the maṣdar of kind (al-maṣdar al-nawʿī); the well-known view is that it is permissible, so one says ضربت ضربين: ضربا عنيفا وضربا رفيقا ("I struck two strikes: a violent strike and a gentle strike"), and ضربت ضروبا مختلفة. The apparent position of Sībawayh is that it is not allowed, and that only what is heard from the Arabs is said. Whoever permits it argues from its occurrence in eloquent speech, as in His saying, the Exalted: «وتظنون بالله الظنونا». They said: the "thought" was made plural only because of the difference in its kinds, since the one whose faith was pure thought that what Allah had promised them of victory was true; the one whose faith was weak had his thought waver; and the one who was a hypocrite thought that the turn of fortune would be against the believers — and their thoughts proved false. Ibn Mālik pointed to this in his saying in al-Khulāṣa:
وما لتوكيد فوحد أبدا ... وثنّ واجمع غيره وأفردا
(What is for emphasis, always keep singular; make the other dual and plural, and singular too.)
3- The readers differed over this alif in (الظنونا). Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr kept it both in continuous recitation and in pause, and this reading is also reported from Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī. They held fast to the script of the ʿUthmānic muṣḥaf and of all the copies in all the lands, for the alif is present in all of them. Abū ʿUbayd chose this reading, except that he said: the reciter should not run the recitation on after them, but should pause on them. They also held fast to what occurs like this in the poetry of the Arabs. Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, al-Jaḥdarī and Yaʿqūb read it with the alif dropped in both continuous recitation and pause, and said it is one of the additions of the script, written thus but not to be pronounced; as for poetry, what is not allowed elsewhere is allowed in it out of necessity. Ibn Kathīr, al-Kisāʾī and Ibn Muḥayṣin [Translator's note: the source writes «ابن محيص»] read it with the alif kept in pause and dropped in continuous recitation, and this reading is preferable with respect to the Arabic language. This alif is what the grammarians call alif al-iṭlāq (the alif of prolongation), and the discussion of it is well known. In the same way the readers differed over the alif in His sayings (الرسولا) and (السبيلا), as will come at the end of this sura.

dervis-irab:57-59.t:
* Vocabulary:
(جَلَابِيبِهِنَّ): al-jalābīb are wraps (malāḥif); the singular is جلبات [Translator's note: the source has جلبات here; the usual singular is جلباب, as the following quotations show]. A woman of Hudhayl said, elegising a slain man:
تمشي النسور إليه وهي لاهية ... مشي العذارى عليهن الجلابيب
(The vultures walk to him unconcerned, as maidens walk wearing their wraps.)
And Abū al-Ṭayyib [al-Mutanabbī] said:
من الجآذر في زي الأعاريب ... حمر الحلي والمطايا والجلابيب
(Of the young wild calves in the garb of Bedouins, red of ornaments, mounts and wraps.)
In al-Qāmūs and elsewhere: «الجلباب, and الجلبّاب with the first bāʾ doubled, is the shirt or the wide garment». In al-Kashshāf: «The jilbāb is a wide garment, wider than the head-cover (khimār) and smaller than the cloak (ridāʾ), which the woman winds over her head, leaving part of it to hang down over her chest».

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ فِي الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةِ): إن and its noun; the clause يؤذون الله ورسوله is the ṣila (relative clause). The meaning of harming Allah and His Messenger is doing what angers them. The clause لعنهم الله is the khabar (predicate) of إن, and في الدنيا والآخرة is attached (mutaʿalliq) to لعنهم.
(وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ عَذاباً مُهِيناً): conjoined to the khabar clause; عذابا is the object of أعد, and لهم is attached to أعد.
(وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ بِغَيْرِ مَا اكْتَسَبُوا): الذين is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause يؤذون المؤمنين والمؤمنات is the ṣila; بغير is attached to يؤذون; ما is relative or maṣdarī, and in either case it, or the maṣdar, is the muḍāf ilayhi of غير.
(فَقَدِ احْتَمَلُوا بُهْتاناً وَإِثْماً مُبِيناً): the fāʾ is linking, because of the hint of condition in the relative noun; قد is a particle of realisation; احتملوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the khabar of الذين. بهتانا is the object of احتملوا; إثما is conjoined to بهتانا; مبينا is an adjective.
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ قُلْ لِأَزْواجِكَ وَبَناتِكَ وَنِساءِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): a resumptive statement, introduced to command those targeted for harm to do what keeps harm away from them, namely covering. لأزواجك is attached to قل, and what follows is conjoined to it.
(يُدْنِينَ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِنْ جَلَابِيبِهِنَّ ذلِكَ أَدْنى أَنْ يُعْرَفْنَ فَلا يُؤْذَيْنَ): the clause يدنين is [the answer to] an omitted maqūl al-qawl (the quoted speech), indicated by its answer, i.e. say to them أرنيه [Translator's note: so in the source; the intended implied speech is presumably «أدنين» (draw down)]. It may also be jussive as the answer to the command. They also allowed يدنين to mean ليدنين, so that it is jussive by the lām of command, and this would then be the quoted speech itself. A discussion of a parallel case was given in detail in al-Raʿd, so refer back to it. عليهن is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and من جلابيبهن is attached to يدنين as its object. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: what is the meaning of من in جلابيبهن? I say: it is partitive, except that the partitive sense allows two interpretations. One is that they wrap themselves in some of the jalābīb they have, the intent being that the free woman should not go about in common dress, in a shift and head-cover, like the slave-girl and the maid (al-māhina), while she has two or more jilbābs in her house. The second is that the woman lets down part of her jilbāb and its excess over her face, veiling herself, so that she is distinguished from the slave-girl». His word الماهنة is the feminine of الماهن, which is the servant. ذلك is a mubtadaʾ and أدنى the khabar; the interpreted maṣdar أن يعرفن is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. nearer to their being recognised. The fāʾ is a conjunction, لا is negative, and يعرفن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn because it is joined to the nūn of the feminine plural, and it is conjoined to أن يعرفن. [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb meant here is يؤذين.]
(وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً): the wāw is a conjunction; كان, its noun and its two khabars.

dervis-irab:14-17.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ دُخِلَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ أَقْطارِها ثُمَّ سُئِلُوا الْفِتْنَةَ لَآتَوْها): the wāw is a conjunction; (دخلت) is a past verb in the passive; (عليهم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) it; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, i.e. the city, or their houses. (من أقطارها) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. from all its sides. (ثم) is a conjunction denoting delay; (سئلوا) is a past verb in the passive, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; (الفتنة) is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (سئلوا), and what is meant by the fitna is apostasy and returning to disbelief. The lām occurs in the apodosis (jawāb) of (لو); (أتوها) is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause has no grammatical position. (وَما تَلَبَّثُوا بِها إِلَّا يَسِيراً): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (تلبثوا) is a past verb and its fāʿil; (بها) is attached to (تلبثوا); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (يسيرا) is the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar or of an omitted time, so it may validly be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or an adverb of time. (وَلَقَدْ كانُوا عاهَدُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ قَبْلُ لا يُوَلُّونَ الْأَدْبارَ وَكانَ عَهْدُ اللَّهِ مَسْؤُلًا): the wāw is a conjunction, the lām prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam), and (قد) is a particle of verification. (كانوا) is a defective past verb and the wāw is its noun; the clause (عاهدوا) is its khabar (predicate); the Divine Name is the mafʿūl bihi; (من قبل) is attached to (عاهدوا). The clause (يولون الأدبار) has no grammatical position, because it is the answer to the oath; (الأدبار) is the second mafʿūl bihi of (يولون), the first being omitted, i.e. they would not turn their backs to the enemy. The wāw is a conjunction; (كان) with its noun and its khabar, i.e. (مسؤولا) meaning "demanded".
(قُلْ لَنْ يَنْفَعَكُمُ الْفِرارُ إِنْ فَرَرْتُمْ مِنَ الْمَوْتِ أَوِ الْقَتْلِ وَإِذاً لا تُمَتَّعُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا): (لن) is a particle of negation, of the accusative and of the future; (ينفعكم) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by (لن), the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi, and (الفرار) is the fāʿil. (إن) is a conditional particle that puts two verbs in the jussive; (فررتم) is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes. (من الموت) is attached to (فررتم). (إذن) is a particle of answer and requital, made inoperative because it occurs after a conjunction, as is usual with it. (لا) is negating; (تمتعون) is an imperfect verb in the passive and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (قليلا) is the naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "except a little enjoyment", or the adjective of an omitted adverb, i.e. "except a little time"; so it may validly be a mafʿūl muṭlaq or an adverb of time. (قُلْ مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَعْصِمُكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ إِنْ أَرادَ بِكُمْ سُوءاً أَوْ أَرادَ بِكُمْ رَحْمَةً): (من) is an interrogative noun, the mubtadaʾ (subject); (ذا) is a demonstrative in the position of a nominative as the khabar; (الذي) is a badal (substitute), and the clause (يعصمكم من الله) is the ṣila (relative clause). (إن) is conditional; (أراد) is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis, and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "then who is it that will protect you?" (سوءا) is the mafʿūl bihi. (أو أراد بكم رحمة) is conjoined to what precedes, and an omitted element must be assumed, i.e. "or [who is it that will] strike you with harm if He wills mercy for you". (وَلا يَجِدُونَ لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَلِيًّا وَلا نَصِيراً): the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; (لا) is negating; (يجدون) is a verb and its fāʿil; (لهم) is in the position of an accusative as the second object of (يجدون); (من دون الله) is a ḥāl; (وليا) is the first mafʿūl bihi, and (ولا نصيرا) is conjoined to (وليا).

dervis-irab:54-56.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنْ تُبْدُوا شَيْئاً أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيماً): إن is conditional; تبدوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and شيئا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). أو تخفوه is conjoined to تبدوا; it is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi. فإن الله: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); إن and its noun, and the clause كان is its khabar (predicate). بكل شيء is attached (mutaʿalliq) to عليما, and عليما is the khabar of كان.
(لا جُناحَ عَلَيْهِنَّ فِي آبائِهِنَّ): لا is the lā of generic negation; جناح is the noun of لا and عليهن its khabar; في آبائهن is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. there is no sin on them in not veiling themselves from these.
(وَلا أَبْنائِهِنَّ وَلا إِخْوانِهِنَّ وَلا أَبْناءِ إِخْوانِهِنَّ وَلا أَبْناءِ أَخَواتِهِنَّ وَلا نِسائِهِنَّ وَلا ما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُهُنَّ): conjoined to what precedes. The meaning of His words ولا نسائهن is: nor is there any blame on the wives of the Prophet in not veiling themselves from their women, i.e. the Muslim women.
(وَاتَّقِينَ اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيداً): the wāw is a conjunction, and اتقين is an imperative verb conjoined to something omitted, i.e. comply with what you have been commanded. واتقين الله is by way of iltifāt (shift) from the third person to direct address; the secret of this shift will come in the Rhetoric section. [The fāʿil is] the nūn of the feminine plural, and the Divine Name is a mafʿūl bihi. إن and its noun; the clause كان, with its latent noun and its khabar, is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إن.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَمَلائِكَتَهُ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ): a resumptive statement, introduced to honour him ﷺ in life and in death. إن and its noun; ملائكته is conjoined to الله; the clause يصلون على النبي is the khabar of إن.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا صَلُّوا عَلَيْهِ وَسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيماً): تسليما is an emphatic maṣdar (mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object).

dervis-irab:60-63.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْمُرْجِفُونَ): In al-Asās he said: «أرجفوا في المدينة بكذا: when they spread news of it in order to throw people into agitation, without its being sound in their view. This is among the rumours (arājīf) of the misguided, and rumour-mongering (irjāf) is the prelude to the event. You say:
إذا وقعت المخاويف كثرت الأراجيف (When fears befall, rumours multiply)». Another source has the following wording:
«أرجف: specific to bad news and seditions, intending to stir people up. أرجف القوم بالشيء and فيه: they plunged into it. أرجفت الريح الشجر: it shook it. أُرجفت الأرض, in the passive: it was struck by an earthquake. The root sense of al-irjāf is shaking, taken from al-rajfa, which is the earthquake; false news is described by it because it is shaky and unstable».
The sea was called rajjāf because of its agitation, and from this is the poet's saying:
المطعون اللحم كلّ عشية ... حتى تغيب الشمس في الرّجاف
(Those who feed meat every evening, until the sun sets into the heaving sea.)
(مَلْعُونِينَ): In al-Asās and al-Lisān he said: «لعنه أهله: his people drove him out and put him far away; he is laʿīn, an outcast. Allah cursed Iblīs: He drove him out of Paradise and put him far from the neighbourhood of the angels. لعنت الكلب والذئب: I drove them both away; the wolf is called al-laʿīn. لعّنه, and he is mulaʿʿan: he cursed him much. تلاعن القوم, تلعّنوا and التعنوا; التعن فلان: he cursed himself. A man who is luʿna and laʿana, like ḍuḥka and ḍuḥaka [one who is cursed by people / one who curses much]. Do not be laʿʿān, i.e. a reviler. لاعن امرأته [he performed the mutual cursing with his wife], and the judge conducted the mutual cursing between them; al-liʿān took place between them, and they cursed one another (تلاعنا والتعنا). Among the figurative usages: أبيت اللعن, which was the greeting of kings in the Jāhiliyya, i.e. may you not do anything that would bring on cursing; and so-and-so is mulaʿʿan al-qidr (his cooking-pot is cursed). Zuhayr said:
ومرهّق النيران يحمد في اللأ ... واء غير ملعّن القدر
(One whose fires are sought by guests, praised in hardship, his cooking-pot not cursed.)
He set up al-laʿīn in his field, which is the scarecrow; and the accursed tree: everyone who tasted it cursed it and hated it».
(ثُقِفُوا): they were found and overtaken. In al-Asās: «We sought him and ثقفناه in such a place, i.e. we caught him. ثقفت العلم أو الصناعة in the quickest time: when you are quick in acquiring it. A boy who is thaqf laqf and thaqif laqif [quick to grasp and to catch]; he has become skilful (thaqufa thaqāfa). ثاقفه مثاقفة: he sported with him with weapons, which is trying to catch the other off guard in sword-play and the like; so-and-so is of the people of muthāqafa, and he is a muthāqif: good at thiqāf with the sword, with kasra. They fenced with one another and so-and-so was the most skilful of them. خلّ ثقيف and ثقّيف: sharp vinegar; in Kitāb al-ʿAyn: ثقيف, and it has become sharp (thaqufa thaqāfa). Among the figurative usages: he educated him and refined him (ثقّفه); were it not for your refining and guiding me I would have been nothing; was I cultivated and refined except at your hand?». The wording of al-Qāmūs: «ثقف, like karuma and fariḥa, thaqfan, thaqafan and thaqāfatan: he became skilful, nimble and astute; so he is thaqf, like ḥibr, thaqif, like katif, and thaqīf, like amīr».

* I'rab:
(لَئِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهِ الْمُنافِقُونَ وَالَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ): the lām prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); إن is conditional; لم is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; ينته is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and it stands as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). المنافقون is its fāʿil (agent); الذين is conjoined to المنافقون; في قلوبهم is a fronted khabar (predicate) and مرض a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
(وَالْمُرْجِفُونَ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ لَنُغْرِيَنَّكَ بِهِمْ): والمرجفون is also conjoined, thereby completing the three descriptions of one thing; for they were three kinds: among them the hypocrites, the people of depravity sick of heart, and those who spread evil reports about the expeditions of the Messenger of Allah — or it is general, covering every rumour-mongering and fabrication of evil reports. في المدينة is attached (mutaʿalliq) to المرجفون. The lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath. نغرينك is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "نحن"; the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and بهم is attached to نغرينك.
(ثُمَّ لا يُجاوِرُونَكَ فِيها إِلَّا قَلِيلًا): ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay. The conjunction indicating delay was preferred only because expulsion from their homelands was graver for them than everything else that befell them, so its status is distanced from the status of what it is conjoined to. In it there is an indication that one who is lawfully required to vacate a dwelling owned by another is given respite while he moves himself, his goods and his family, for a period of time until he obtains another dwelling, according to [the judge's] discretion. لا is negative; يجاورونك is an imperfect verb conjoined to نغرينك, so it is nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and the kāf its object. فيها is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). إلا is a particle of restriction, and قليلا is an adverb of time attached to يجاورونك, or a maṣdar — i.e. except a [little] neighbouring — i.e. a short time while they depart and gather themselves and their families.
(مَلْعُونِينَ أَيْنَما ثُقِفُوا أُخِذُوا وَقُتِّلُوا تَقْتِيلًا): ملعونين is a ḥāl of something implied which has been omitted together with its governing word, i.e. then they will go out [accursed]; or of the fāʿil of يجاورونك, the particle of exception having entered upon the adverb and the ḥāl together, as in His words «إلا أن يؤذن لكم إلى طعام غير ناظرين إناه». Al-Zamakhsharī said:
«It is not valid for it to be made accusative by أخذوا, because what comes after the conditional word does not govern what comes before it. It has been said of قليلا that it too is accusative as a ḥāl, its meaning being: they will not be your neighbours except as few, humiliated and accursed». Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ allowed it to be made accusative by أخذوا, because they both allow the governed word of the apodosis to be put before the conditional particle, as in: خيرا إن تأتيني تصب. أينما is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place (ẓarfiyya makāniyya), and it is attached to أخذوا, i.e. to its apodosis. ثقفوا is a passive past verb, in the position of the jussive as the protasis; أخذوا is also a passive past verb, and it is the apodosis; قتلوا is a passive past verb, and تقتيلا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
(سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ فِي الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا): سنة الله is in the position of the accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. it is an emphatic maṣdar, i.e. Allah has laid down concerning those who act hypocritically that they be killed wherever they are caught. في الذين is a ḥāl; the clause خلوا is the ṣila; من قبل is attached to خلوا. ولن: the wāw is a conjunction, though you may make it circumstantial; لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; تجد is an imperfect verb, accusative by لن; لسنة الله is attached to تبديلا; تبديلا is a mafʿūl bihi.
(يَسْئَلُكَ النَّاسُ عَنِ السَّاعَةِ): a resumptive statement, introduced to relate the state of the mockers among the polytheists and the Jews, who used to ask the Prophet about the Hour, seeking to hasten it by way of mockery. يسألك is an imperfect verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi; الناس is the fāʿil; عن الساعة is attached to يسألك.
(قُلْ إِنَّما عِلْمُها عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): إنما is the restraining [ما] and the restrained [إن] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); علمها is a mubtadaʾ, and عند الله is an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar.
(وَما يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّ السَّاعَةَ تَكُونُ قَرِيباً): the wāw is a conjunction; ما is an interrogative noun of disapproval, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause يدريك is its khabar. لعل and its noun, and the clause تكون is its khabar; the clause is suspended (muʿallaqa) by the interrogative, so it is in the position of the accusative as a second object. قريبا is the khabar of تكون, on the basis that the qualified noun is omitted, i.e. something near. وقل قريبا [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably وقيل, "It has been said"]: its use as an adverb has become frequent, so here it is an adverb in the position of the khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī indicated the two views by saying: «قريبا: something near; or because the Hour has the sense of the Day; or [it means] at a near time».

dervis-irab:64-68.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سادَتَنا): a broken plural on the pattern faʿala, with two fatḥas. This pattern is common for an adjective describing a rational masculine being whose final radical is sound, as كامل / كملة, ساحر / سحرة, سافر / سفرة and بار / بررة. Allah the Exalted said: «وجاء السحرة» and «بأيدي سفرة، كرام بررة». The condition "adjective" excludes the noun, as واد and باز; "masculine" excludes words like حائض and طالق; "rational" excludes words like سابق and لاحق as descriptions of two horses; and "sound final radical" excludes words like قاض and غاز. None of these is regularly pluralised on faʿala with two fatḥas. It occurs anomalously with words not of the pattern fāʿil, as سيد / سادة, whose pattern is faʿala. It may also be the plural of سائد, like فاجر / فجرة and كافر / كفرة, and this is closer to analogy, as you have seen. Yet the author of al-Qāmūs did not keep to the rule, for he said: «al-sāʾid is the master, or one below him, and the plural is سادة and سيايد». Ibn ʿĀmir read ساداتنا, pluralising it a second time with alif and tāʾ, and this too is not according to analogy.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَنَ الْكافِرِينَ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ سَعِيراً): إن and its noun, and the clause لعن الكافرين is its khabar (predicate). أعد is conjoined to لعن; لهم is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أعدّ; سعيرا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Al-saʿīr is the fire that is kindled, intensely blazing, and for that reason the pronoun referring to it is feminine.
(خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً لا يَجِدُونَ وَلِيًّا وَلا نَصِيراً): a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الكافرين. فيها is attached to خالدين, and أبدا is an adverb of time also attached to خالدين. The clause لا يجدون is a second ḥāl; وليا is the object of يجدون, and ولا نصيرا is conjoined to وليا.
(يَوْمَ تُقَلَّبُ وُجُوهُهُمْ فِي النَّارِ يَقُولُونَ يا لَيْتَنا أَطَعْنَا اللَّهَ وَأَطَعْنَا الرَّسُولَا): يوم is an adverb of time attached to يقولون, or attached to an omitted verb whose implied form is "اذكر" (remember). Abū al-Baqāʾ attached it to His words لا يجدون or to نصيرا. The clause تقلب is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; it is a passive imperfect verb, and وجوههم is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); في النار is attached to تقلب. The clause يقولون is either resumptive or a ḥāl of the pronoun in وجوههم or of the faces themselves. The secret of singling out the faces and the meaning of their being turned will come in the Rhetoric section. يا is a particle of alerting, or a vocative particle with the one addressed omitted. ليت and its noun, and the clause أطعنا الله is its khabar; وأطعنا الرسولا is conjoined to أطعنا الله.
(وَقالُوا رَبَّنا إِنَّا أَطَعْنا سادَتَنا وَكُبَراءَنا فَأَضَلُّونَا السَّبِيلَا): a resumptive statement, introduced to lay out an excuse for themselves. You may also conjoin it to يقولون, by way of turning from the imperfect to the past to indicate that this saying of theirs is not continuous like their previous saying, but is a kind of excuse that is neither valid nor accepted. ربنا is a vocative in construct (munādā muḍāf); إن and its noun, and the clause أطعنا سادتنا وكبراءنا is its khabar. فأضلونا is conjoined to أطعنا; أضلونا is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and first mafʿūl bihi, and السبيلا is the second mafʿūl bihi; one says ضل السبيل and أضله إياه. The alif is added to prolong the sound; the verse-endings were made like the rhymes of poetry, and its benefit is the pause and the indication that the speech has ended and that what follows is resumptive.
(رَبَّنا آتِهِمْ ضِعْفَيْنِ مِنَ الْعَذابِ وَالْعَنْهُمْ لَعْناً كَبِيراً): آتهم is an imperative verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a first mafʿūl bihi; ضعفين is the second mafʿūl bihi; من العذاب is an adjective of ضعفين. العنهم is an imperative verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; لعنا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and كبيرا is a naʿt (adjective) of لعنا.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «يوم تقلب وجوههم في النار», the faces are singled out for mention because the face is above all the other limbs, and it stands as that which confronts [others]. The meaning of their being turned is their being turned about in different directions, like meat roasted in the fire, or [like something] placed in the water of a pot while it is boiling, so that the boiling tosses it to every side.

dervis-irab:18-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْمُعَوِّقِينَ): those who discourage, who used to let the Muslims down. In al-Asās: «عاقه, اعتاقه and عوّقه (he hindered him): "قد يعلم الله المعوّقين منكم". And you say: "So-and-so kept company with hindrance (التعويق), so success (التوفيق) abandoned him." A man who is عُوَقة is one given to hindering and holding back from good. And you say: "O you who holds back from good, the most fitting of your names is 'ʿAwwaq'."» [Translator's note: the last phrase is a pun in the Arabic, «أن تعوق», which may be read as the idol's name Yaʿūq/ʿAwūq or as "that you hinder".]
(أَشِحَّةً): plural of (شحيح), the miserly and covetous. It is a non-analogical plural, because the analogical plural of the adjective of the pattern فعيل whose second and third radicals are of the same kind (i.e. doubled) is أفعلاء, as in خليل / أخلاء and ظنين / أظناء; and أشحاء has been heard, which is the analogical form.
(سَلَقُوكُمْ): they hurt you, or harmed you. In al-Mukhtār: «سلقه بالكلام: he hurt him with words, which is harshness of speech with the tongue; the Exalted said: "سلقوكم بألسنة حداد". سلق البقل أو البيض: he boiled the herbs or the eggs lightly over the fire. All of them are of the conjugation of ضرب.» In al-Miṣbāḥ it is also of the conjugation of قتل. Al-Rāghib's wording: «السلق is stretching out with force, either with the hand or with the tongue.» And it is taken from al-Qāmūs and al-Lisān: سلق, يسلق, of the conjugation of قتل: he boiled the eggs or the herbs over the fire and cooked them in water; سلقه بالكلام: he hurt him — and from this, سلقه بألسنة حداد; سلقه بالرمح: he pierced him with the spear; سلقه بالسوط: he whipped him until he stripped off his skin; سلق اللحم عن العظم: he peeled the meat off the bone. The expression may be figurative, as will come in the section on rhetoric. In any case, the common people use this word in a way that is beyond reproach.

* I'rab:
(قَدْ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ الْمُعَوِّقِينَ مِنْكُمْ وَالْقائِلِينَ لِإِخْوانِهِمْ هَلُمَّ إِلَيْنا): resumptive speech, introduced to depict the state of the hypocrites. (قد) is a particle of multiplicity, though its basic sense is paucity when it enters an imperfect verb; its discussion has preceded. (يعلم الله المعوقين) is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (منكم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (القائلين) is conjoined to (المعوقين); (لإخوانهم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (القائلين). (هلم) is a verbal noun with imperative meaning, and (إلينا) is attached to it. This is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz, who make it the same for the singular and the plural; it is used intransitively, as here, and transitively, as in al-Anʿām, and the discussion of it has preceded. (وَلا يَأْتُونَ الْبَأْسَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا): the wāw is circumstantial; (لا) is negating; (يأتون البأس) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi — i.e. the fighting; (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and (قليلا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or an adverb of time. (أَشِحَّةً عَلَيْكُمْ فَإِذا جاءَ الْخَوْفُ رَأَيْتَهُمْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَيْكَ): (أشحة) is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of (يأتون), or accusative in censure by an omitted verb, its implied form being "I censure" (أذم). Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «أشحة عليكم: at the time of war, sparing of you [Translator's note: the source has «أضناء», apparently for «أضنّاء»], hovering over you as a man does over the one who defends him and fights on his behalf at a time of fear.» (فإذا): the fāʾ is resumptive, and (إذا) is a future adverb including the sense of condition; the clause (جاء الخوف) is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it. The clause (رأيتهم) has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. The clause (ينظرون إليك) is a ḥāl, because the seeing here is visual; (إليك) is attached to (ينظرون).
(تَدُورُ أَعْيُنُهُمْ كَالَّذِي يُغْشى عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْمَوْتِ): the clause (تدور أعينهم) is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of (ينظرون), which is the wāw. (كالذي) is the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "they roll a rolling like the rolling of the eye of the one who…"; so after the kāf two things are omitted: "rolling" and "eye". The clause (يغشى) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذي). (يغشى) is an imperfect verb in the passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is the pronoun of a maṣdar, made specific by the lām of prior reference or by an omitted adjective, the meaning being "the familiar swooning comes over him"; (عليه) is attached to (يغشى). The nāʾib fāʿil may also be the preposition with its genitive noun; the discussion of what stands in for the nāʾib fāʿil has preceded, so refresh your memory of it. (فَإِذا ذَهَبَ الْخَوْفُ سَلَقُوكُمْ بِأَلْسِنَةٍ حِدادٍ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (إذا) is a future adverb including the sense of condition; the clause (ذهب الخوف) is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it. The clause (سلقوكم) is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position; (بألسنة) is attached to (سلقوكم), and (حداد) is the naʿt of (ألسنة).
(أَشِحَّةً عَلَى الْخَيْرِ أُولئِكَ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا فَأَحْبَطَ اللَّهُ أَعْمالَهُمْ وَكانَ ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيراً): (أشحة) is accusative as a ḥāl or in censure, as preceded. (على الخير) is attached to (أشحة), i.e. greedy for the booty, seeking it. (أولئك) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause (لم يؤمنوا) is the khabar (predicate). (فأحبط) is conjoined to (لم يؤمنوا); (الله) is the fāʿil and (أعمالهم) the mafʿūl bihi. (وكان): the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; (كان) with its noun and its khabar; (على الله) is a ḥāl. The demonstrative refers to the nullifying, and the meaning is that their deeds deserve to be nullified, with nothing to avert it, and it is not a hard or difficult matter.

* Rhetoric:
1- The device of al-tandīr (the witty touch):
In His saying «فإذا جاء الخوف رأيتهم ينظرون إليك تدور أعينهم كالذي يغشى عليه الموت» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads «يُغْشى عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْمَوْتِ»] there is a device alluded to by the author of Nihāyat al-Arab and by Ibn Abī al-Iṣbaʿ, namely the device of al-tandīr. Its definition is that the speaker brings a sweet rarity or a delightful witticism. It occurs in both earnest and jest; it does not fall within the scope of sarcasm, nor within the scope of the jest that intends earnest, but it may fall within the scope of hyperbole. That is clear in the Exalted's hyperbole in describing the hypocrites with fear and cowardice, where He reported of them that their eyes roll while looking, like the state of one who swoons from death. Had He confined Himself to saying "like one who swoons" it would have sufficed for the purpose, but He added something by saying «من الموت», since the state of one swooning from death is more severe and more grievous than the state of one swooning from something other than death. Had He, glory be to Him, put "fear" in place of "death", the speech would certainly have been eloquent; yet what came in the Revelation is more eloquent. It is, moreover, framed as truth and set in the place of veracity, for whoever is strong of soul and brave of heart does not accept hypocrisy, but openly shows what the fearful one conceals, because he does not care about death.
2- The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya):
That is in His saying «سلقوكم بألسنة حداد»: He likened the tongue to a sword, then omitted the thing compared to and borrowed one of its properties, namely striking. This metaphor holds on the interpretation of السلق as striking, and what prompts it is the description of the tongues as sharp, as preceded in the section on vocabulary.

dervis-irab:20-22.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بادُونَ): plural of (باد), a dweller of the desert. One says: "You have gone to the desert (بدوت), so-and-so", i.e. you have settled in the desert and become a Bedouin; "What have you to do with Bedouin life?"; and "the town-dweller became a Bedouin (تبدّى)". One says: "Where are the people?" and you say: "They have gone out to the desert (لقد بدوا)", i.e. they went out to the open country — they had a few sheep they would go out to.
(الْأَعْرابِ): He said in al-Qāmūs and its commentary: al-ʿurb, with ḍamma, and al-ʿarab, with fatḥa on both letters, are the opposite of the non-Arabs (al-ʿajam); it is feminine. They are the inhabitants of the towns, or it is general; and al-aʿrāb among them are the inhabitants of the desert; it has no singular, and its plural is أعاريب. "ʿArab ʿāriba", "ʿarbāʾ" and "ʿaraba" are pure Arabs; "mutaʿarriba" and "mustaʿriba" are those who entered among them.

* I'rab:
(يَحْسَبُونَ الْأَحْزابَ لَمْ يَذْهَبُوا وَإِنْ يَأْتِ الْأَحْزابُ يَوَدُّوا لَوْ أَنَّهُمْ بادُونَ فِي الْأَعْرابِ): the speech is resumptive, introduced to depict their fear. You may make it a ḥāl (circumstantial) from one of the preceding pronouns, i.e. from fear they are like those who cannot believe that the Confederates have gone away from them and abandoned supporting them.
(يحسبون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الأحزاب) is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause (لم يذهبوا) is the second mafʿūl bihi. (وإن): the wāw is a conjunction and (إن) is conditional; (يأت) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; (الأحزاب) is the fāʿil; (يودوا) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn. (لو) is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar); (لو) and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar that is the object of (يودوا), i.e. because of their fear of what they have been afflicted with they wish their being [Translator's note: the source has «أشرتهم», which appears corrupt; perhaps «كونهم»] out in the desert. And (أن) with what falls in its domain is interpreted as a maṣdar that is the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being "they would wish that it were established that they are in the desert". More discussion of maṣdariyya (لو) will come in the section on benefits. (أن) with its noun, and (بادون) is its khabar (predicate); (في الأعراب) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (بادون), or to an omitted ḥāl.
(يَسْئَلُونَ عَنْ أَنْبائِكُمْ وَلَوْ كانُوا فِيكُمْ ما قاتَلُوا إِلَّا قَلِيلًا): the clause (يسألون) may be resumptive, or a ḥāl from the pronoun of (يحسبون). (عن أنبائكم) is attached to (يسألون). The wāw is circumstantial; (لو) is conditional; (كان) with its noun, and (فيكم) is its khabar. (ما) is negating; (قاتلوا) is a verb and its fāʿil; the clause (ما قاتلوا) has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. What we set out regarding His saying «ولو أن ما في البحر من شجرة أقلام» — the verse — applies to it. (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and (قليلا) is the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "except a little fighting", or the naʿt of an omitted adverb, i.e. "except a little time".
(لَقَدْ كانَ لَكُمْ فِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ): resumptive speech, introduced to reproach those who stayed behind from fighting. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath, and (قد) is a particle of verification. (كان) is a defective past verb; (لكم) is its fronted khabar; (في رسول الله) is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of (أسوة); (أسوة) is the delayed noun of (كان), and (حسنة) is an adjective of (أسوة), i.e. a good example — with ḍamma on the hamza, and it may take kasra.
(لِمَنْ كانَ يَرْجُوا اللَّهَ وَالْيَوْمَ الْآخِرَ وَذَكَرَ اللَّهَ كَثِيراً): (لمن): the preposition with its genitive noun is a badal (substitute) from (لكم), the lām being repeated with the badal for separation; or it is a badal al-ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion). The clause (كان) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (من); the noun of (كان) is latent, its implied form being "he", and the clause (يرجو الله) is its khabar. (اليوم الآخر) is conjoined to the Divine Name; (ذكر) is conjoined to (كان); the Divine Name is the mafʿūl bihi, and (كثيرا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or an adverb; its like has preceded shortly.
(وَلَمَّا رَأَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْأَحْزابَ قالُوا: هذا ما وَعَدَنَا اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ): (لما) is a temporal adverb (ḥīniyya) attached to (قالوا), or a linking particle including the sense of condition, in either case. (رأى المؤمنون الأحزاب) is a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause (قالوا) has no grammatical position. (هذا) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (ما) the khabar, and the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying); the clause (وعدنا الله ورسوله) is the ṣila of (ما). (وَصَدَقَ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ وَما زادَهُمْ إِلَّا إِيماناً وَتَسْلِيماً): the wāw is a conjunction; (صدق الله) is a verb and its fāʿil. In it the overt noun is put in place of the pronoun, to magnify Him and to draw attention to the promise of the two of them that came to pass. (وما زادهم) is conjoined to (صدق); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (إيمانا) is the second mafʿūl bihi of (زادهم), and (تسليما) is conjoined to (إيمانا). The fāʿil of (زادهم) is the pronoun of the promise, or of the truthfulness.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «وصدق الله ورسوله» there is the device of repeating the overt noun out of veneration. Had He repeated the two as pronouns, He would have combined the name of Allah the Exalted and the name of His Messenger in one word, saying «وصدقا» ("and the two were truthful"). The Prophet disliked that, when he answered one of the preachers who spoke before him, who said: "Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger is rightly guided, and whoever disobeys the two of them (يعصهما) has gone astray." The Prophet said to him: "What a bad preacher of the people you are! Say: 'and whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger'", aiming to magnify Allah. Some scholars found a difficulty in his saying, upon him be blessing and peace, "until Allah and His Messenger are more beloved to him than anything besides the two of them (سواهما)", saying that he combined them in a single pronoun. This difficulty was answered by saying that the Prophet ﷺ knows Allah's due better than we do, so it is not for us to say as he says.

* Benefits:
Maṣdariyya (لو):
Maṣdariyya (لو) is synonymous with maṣdariyya (أن) in meaning and in forming a maṣdar, except that it does not put the verb in the accusative. It occurs mostly after something with the sense of wishing, such as ودّ, أحب, اختار and تمنى; and it is said, rather, specifically after ودّ and تمنى, because a person may love a thing yet not wish for its occurrence owing to some obstacle in seeking it. It occurs after other than wishing rarely, as in the saying of Qutayla — in the diminutive form — daughter of al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith al-Asadiyya, addressing the Prophet ﷺ when he had her father al-Naḍr killed in captivity (ṣabran) after returning from the Battle of Badr:
ما كان ضرك المن لو مننت وربما ... منّ الفتى وهو المغيظ المحنق
(What harm would it have done you had you shown grace? Often a young man shows grace though enraged and furious.)
i.e. "what would grace have harmed you" [Translator's note: the source glosses the verse as «ما كان ضرك المن», showing the maṣdar meaning of «لو مننت»]. Before this verse is:
أمحمد ولأنت فحل نجيبة ... في قومها والفحل فحل معرق
(O Muhammad — you are the scion of a noble mother among her people, and the stallion is of a deep-rooted stallion line.)
The reason the Prophet had her father killed was that he used to read the stories of the Persians to the Arabs, saying: "Muhammad brings you the stories of ʿĀd and Thamūd, and I bring you the story of the Chosroes and the Caesars", intending thereby to hurt the Prophet. When the Prophet heard this verse — one of a set of verses she recited before him — he said: "Had I heard it before his killing, I would not have killed him, and I would have pardoned him." Then he said: "No Qurashī shall be killed in captivity."
Some legal theorists have taken his saying ﷺ "Had I heard it before his killing, I would not have killed him, and I would have pardoned him" as evidence for the permissibility of delegating judgment to the mujtahid — so that it is said to him: "Judge as you will, and it is right" — and for its having actually occurred; for his saying "before his killing" indicates that the killing and its omission were delegated to him. Those who deny its occurrence answer that it is possible the Prophet was given a choice between the two together, so it was said to him: "You may order his killing or not order it", and the like; and it is possible that revelation came down that, had someone interceded for him, he would not have killed him. The نجيبة is the noble, good woman; the فحل is the male of every animal, as in al-Qāmūs; and معرق is the active participle of أعرق الرجل, "the man became deep-rooted", i.e. he has a root in nobility. The meaning of (لو مننت) is "had you bestowed a favour and done good". Then it is possible that the interpreted maṣdar from (لو) and (مننت), i.e. "the grace", is the delayed noun of (كان), and the clause (ضرك) its fronted khabar; and it is possible that the maṣdar is the fāʿil of (ضرك), the clause being the khabar of (كان), whose noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). It is also possible that (ما) is interrogative, its position nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and (كان) may be redundant (zāʾida) or not: on the first, the clause (ضرك) is the khabar of interrogative (ما); on the second, the clause (ضرك) is the khabar of (كان) and the clause of (كان) is the khabar of (ما). Moreover, it is possible that (لو) is conditional in its normal use, with what precedes indicating the apodosis — and that would overturn all of this. (المغيظ), with fatḥa on the mīm, is the passive participle of غاظه يغيظه, with the dotted ghayn and ẓāʾ — the غيظ being anger, or its intensity, or its first onset. (المحنق), with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the nūn, is the passive participle of أحنقه, with the undotted ḥāʾ, when he enraged him.
Returning to the mention of maṣdariyya (لو), we say: maṣdariyya (لو) has no apodosis; when a past verb follows it, it remains past, and when an imperfect verb follows it, it makes it purely future — just as maṣdariyya (أن) does.

dervis-irab:23-27.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قَضى نَحْبَهُ): he died. النحب is a vow (النذر), and their saying "he fulfilled his naḥb" has come to be an expression for death, because every living being must die, so it is as though it were a binding vow upon his neck; when he dies, he has fulfilled his naḥb, i.e. his vow. النذر is with fatḥa on the nūn; the author of al-Munjid erred in vocalising it with kasra, and that is strange. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «نحب نحبا, of the conjugation of ضرب: he wept, and the noun is النحيب; نحب نحبا, of the conjugation of قتل: he vowed. قضى نحبه: he died, or was killed in the way of Allah. In the Revelation: "فمنهم من قضى نحبه".»
(صَياصِيهِمْ): their fortresses; plural of صيصية. In al-Qāmūs: «The صيصية is the weaver's spike with which the warp and weft are evened, the spur on the rooster's leg, the horn of cattle and gazelles, the fortress, and anything by which one is protected.»

* I'rab:
(مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ رِجالٌ صَدَقُوا ما عاهَدُوا اللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ): resumptive speech, introduced to set out the state of the righteous among the Companions who vowed that, if they met a battle alongside the Messenger of Allah, they would stand firm and fight until they were martyred, and to divide them into two groups.
(من المؤمنين) is a fronted khabar (predicate) and (رجال) a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (صدقوا) is an adjective of (رجال); (ما) is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (عاهدوا الله عليه) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما), and (عليه) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (عاهدوا). (فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَضى نَحْبَهُ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَنْتَظِرُ وَما بَدَّلُوا تَبْدِيلًا): the fāʾ is of ramification (tafrīʿ); (منهم) is a fronted khabar and (من) a delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause (قضى نحبه) is the ṣila of (من); (ومنهم من ينتظر) is conjoined to what precedes it. The wāw is a conjunction, (ما) is negating, (بدلوا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the mafʿūl bihi is omitted, i.e. the pledge; (تبديلا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (لِيَجْزِيَ اللَّهُ الصَّادِقِينَ بِصِدْقِهِمْ وَيُعَذِّبَ الْمُنافِقِينَ إِنْ شاءَ): the lām is the lām of cause; (يجزي) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (أن) after the lām. The preposition with its genitive noun is attached to an implied resumptive verb, introduced to explain what brought about the occurrence of the sayings that were narrated, the implied form being "all that occurred, occurred so that Allah may reward the truthful". It is also said to be attached to what precedes it and to follow from it, so that it is attached to (صدقوا), as a cause for it; and other things have been said, but what we have mentioned is preferable. (الله) is the fāʿil, (الصادقين) the mafʿūl bihi, and (بصدقهم) is attached to (يجزي). (ويعذب المنافقين) is conjoined to (ليجزي الله الصادقين). (إن) is conditional; (شاء) is a past verb, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, as is the object of (شاء), i.e. "if He wills to punish them, He punishes them".
(أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً): (أو) is a conjunction and (يتوب) is conjoined to what precedes it; (عليهم) is attached to (يتوب). The clause (إن الله) is a causal explanation of what precedes: (إن) with its noun, and the clause (كان) is its khabar; the noun of (كان) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He"; (غفورا) is its first khabar and (رحيما) its second khabar.
(وَرَدَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِغَيْظِهِمْ لَمْ يَنالُوا خَيْراً): the wāw is a conjunction; (رد الله الذين كفروا) is conjoined to what precedes, and is a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila of the relative noun — they are the Confederates. (بغيظهم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. enraged; you may also make it a second object of (رد). The clause (لم ينالوا خيرا) is a second ḥāl, or a ḥāl from the first ḥāl, so that they are nested (mutadākhila). (وَكَفَى اللَّهُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الْقِتالَ وَكانَ اللَّهُ قَوِيًّا عَزِيزاً): the wāw is a conjunction; (كفى الله المؤمنين) is a verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi, and (القتال) is the second mafʿūl bihi, because (كفى) here means "protected" (وقى), and in that case it is transitive to two objects; the discussion of (كفى) has passed in detail. (كان) with its noun and its two khabars.
(وَأَنْزَلَ الَّذِينَ ظاهَرُوهُمْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ مِنْ صَياصِيهِمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (أنزل) is a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, referring to Allah; (الذين) is the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause (ظاهروهم) is the ṣila; (من أهل الكتاب) is a ḥāl; (من صياصيهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أنزل). You may also make the speech resumptive, introduced [Translator's note: the source has «مسوفا», a misprint for «مسوقا»] to begin narrating the story of the campaign against the Banū Qurayẓa, a summary of which will come in the section on benefits. (وَقَذَفَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الرُّعْبَ فَرِيقاً تَقْتُلُونَ وَتَأْسِرُونَ فَرِيقاً): (وقذف) is conjoined to (أنزل); (في قلوبهم) is attached to (قذف); (الرعب) is the mafʿūl bihi of (قذف); (فريقا) is a fronted object of (تقتلون); (تأسرون فريقا) is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi. (وَأَوْرَثَكُمْ أَرْضَهُمْ وَدِيارَهُمْ وَأَمْوالَهُمْ وَأَرْضاً لَمْ تَطَؤُها وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيراً):
(أورثكم) is a verb, a latent fāʿil and the first mafʿūl bihi; (أرضهم) is the second mafʿūl bihi; (ديارهم), (أموالهم) and (أرضا) are conjoined to (أرضهم); the clause (لم تطئوها) is an adjective of (أرضا); (كان) with its noun and its khabar. What is meant by it [the land not yet trodden] is the lands they conquered later.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ورد الذين كفروا بغيظهم ...» — the verse — there is the device of al-munāsaba (congruity). Allusion to this device has preceded, and that it is of two kinds: congruity in meanings and congruity in wording. What occurs in this verse is of the first kind, because had the speech been confined to what precedes the verse-ending, it would have led some weak people to imagine that this report agrees with the belief of the disbelievers that the wind which arose was the cause of their returning disappointed and of the believers being spared fighting them — that the wind merely arose by chance, as it arises in some of their battles and in their fighting one another — and they would have thought that it was not from Allah. So a safeguard (iḥtirās) was provided by the coming of the verse-ending, in which He, glory be to Him, reported that He is Strong, Mighty, able by His strength to do every impossible thing, that His party is the victorious one, and that by His power He makes victory come to the believers in various forms, to increase them in faith and steadfastness. He grants them victory once through fighting, as on the day of Badr; at another time through the wind, as on the day of the Confederates; at another through terror, as with the Banū al-Naḍīr; sometimes He gives victory against them first and makes the final outcome theirs at last, as on the day of Uḥud; and sometimes He shows them that numbers were not and never will be everything in battle, and how many a small band has overcome a large band, so that they may realise that victory is only from Allah, as on the day of Ḥunayn. This is among the most splendid things with which speech is adorned.

* Benefits:
